before: A condition is a question with a boolean result: true or false. >= means greater than or equal to; == compares values for equality. For these integer examples, neither comparison changes a variable.
if (condition) runs its braced block only when the condition is true. else runs the alternative when it is false.
With seats >= 2, exactly 2 qualifies. The comparison includes equality. A > comparison would exclude 2.
Only one of this if/else pair runs. Continue tracing after the selected block finishes.
after: A condition gives a boolean result: true or false. >= asks whether the left value is greater than or equal to the right value. A comparison checks values without replacing them.
A branch is one possible path through the code. if runs its block when the condition is true. else runs the other block when the condition is false. Braces group each block's instructions.
seats >= 2 allows exactly two seats because >= includes equality. Using > would require more than two. The exact boundary matters.
Only one block in this if/else pair runs. After that block finishes, execution continues after the whole choice.
